---
title: "Gene Ontology Results Excel Export"
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
#| echo: false

pacman::p_load(openxlsx2, readxl, install = FALSE)

conflicted::conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")

# Source the function for adding GO data to Excel
source(here("custom_func/add_go_to_excel_function.R"))
```

## Introduction

This document prepares an Excel file containing the Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment results for the top 1000 and top 2000 CG sites. Each dataset will be placed in a separate sheet with appropriate formatting.

## Load Data

### Load GO results

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# Path to the RDS files
go_path <- here("pathway_analysis/02_gene_ontology/output")

# Read the GO results RDS files
top1000_go <- readRDS(file.path(go_path, "top1000_all_GO_results.rds")) |> 
  # Filter for significant results (p.adjust < 0.05)
  dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05)
top2000_go <- readRDS(file.path(go_path, "top2000_all_GO_results.rds")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(p.adjust < 0.05)


# Check the structure of the data
cat("Top 1000 GO results:\n")
glimpse(top1000_go)
cat("Top 2000 GO results:\n")
glimpse(top2000_go)
```

### Load function categories

```{r}
#| label: load-function-categories

top1000_function_categories <- read_excel(
  here("pathway_analysis/04_function_categorization/output/top1000_condition_specific_GO_terms_auto_cat.xlsx")
)
top2000_function_categories <- read_excel(
  here("pathway_analysis/04_function_categorization/output/top2000_condition_specific_GO_terms_auto_cat.xlsx")
)

# Check the structure of the data
cat("Top 1000 function categories:\n")
glimpse(top1000_function_categories)
cat("Top 2000 function categories:\n")
glimpse(top2000_function_categories)
```

### Load the transition-specific GO terms

The terms significant in only one group, which define the `transition_specific` flag. The flag is set from this list rather than from whether a term received a category, because a term that matched no keyword rule is still significant in only one group.

```{r}
#| label: load-transition-specific-terms

specific_path <- here("pathway_analysis/03_transition_specific_GO_terms/output")

top1000_specific_terms <- read_csv(
  file.path(specific_path, "top1000_condition_specific_GO_terms.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
top2000_specific_terms <- read_csv(
  file.path(specific_path, "top2000_condition_specific_GO_terms.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

top1000_specific_terms |> count(condition)
top2000_specific_terms |> count(condition)
```


### Load the duplicate parents and the specificity weights

The authors' recount (2026-10-09, reviewer R2.9; `pathway_analysis/06_go_hierarchy/03_go_term_weights.qmd`): parent terms whose genes are identical to those of a significant child term (Rule 1) and the redundancy-aware weight of each term significant in only one group (Rule 2; since 2026-10-13 a relative significant in the term's own group lowers the weight as well).

```{r}
#| label: load-weights

source(here("custom_func/go_term_weights.R"))

duplicate_parents <- list(`1000` = read_go_duplicate_parents(1000), `2000` = read_go_duplicate_parents(2000))
term_weights <- list(`1000` = read_go_term_weights(1000), `2000` = read_go_term_weights(2000))
```

## Merge GO results with function categories and weights

Each significant term gets its category, whether it is significant in only one group, and its weight. A duplicate parent stays in the workbook, marked "Removed" and with the child it duplicates in `duplicate_of`, so the sheet remains the full list of significant terms.

```{r}
#| label: merge-go-and-function-categories

add_specificity_columns <- function(go, function_categories, specific_terms, duplicates, weights) {
  go |>
    left_join(select(function_categories, ID, biofunc_category = function_category), by = "ID") |>
    # Is the term significant in only one group?
    left_join(
      specific_terms |> distinct(ID, condition) |> mutate(transition_specific = "Yes"),
      by = c("ID", "condition")
    ) |>
    left_join(select(duplicates, ID = parent, duplicate_of = child), by = "ID") |>
    left_join(
      select(
        weights, condition, ID, n_relatives,
        n_relatives_same_group = n_relatives_same, n_relatives_other_group = n_relatives_other,
        n_relatives_significant, specificity_weight = w
      ),
      by = c("condition", "ID")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      transition_specific = case_when(
        !is.na(duplicate_of) ~ "Removed",
        !is.na(transition_specific) ~ transition_specific,
        .default = "No"
      )
    ) |>
    replace_na(list(biofunc_category = "", duplicate_of = "")) |>
    rename(transition = condition) |>
    relocate(
      transition_specific, duplicate_of, n_relatives, n_relatives_same_group, n_relatives_other_group,
      n_relatives_significant, specificity_weight, biofunc_category,
      .after = last_col()
    )
}

top1000_go_with_categories <- add_specificity_columns(
  top1000_go, top1000_function_categories, top1000_specific_terms, duplicate_parents$`1000`, term_weights$`1000`
)
top2000_go_with_categories <- add_specificity_columns(
  top2000_go, top2000_function_categories, top2000_specific_terms, duplicate_parents$`2000`, term_weights$`2000`
)

# Every transition-specific term is flagged exactly once and has a weight; every
# duplicate parent is marked in each group where it is significant
check_flags <- function(go_with_categories, specific_terms, duplicates, weights) {
  is_yes <- go_with_categories$transition_specific == "Yes"
  all(
    sum(is_yes) == nrow(specific_terms),
    sum(is_yes) == nrow(weights),
    !anyNA(go_with_categories$specificity_weight[is_yes]),
    all(is.na(go_with_categories$specificity_weight[!is_yes])),
    setequal(go_with_categories$ID[go_with_categories$transition_specific == "Removed"], duplicates$parent)
  )
}

stopifnot(
  "top 1000: flags or weights do not match the transition-specific term list" =
    check_flags(top1000_go_with_categories, top1000_specific_terms, duplicate_parents$`1000`, term_weights$`1000`),
  "top 2000: flags or weights do not match the transition-specific term list" =
    check_flags(top2000_go_with_categories, top2000_specific_terms, duplicate_parents$`2000`, term_weights$`2000`)
)

# Flags by group (the text reports 137 normal2mci terms at the top 1,000 and
# 431 terms in all at the top 2,000)
top1000_go_with_categories |> count(transition, transition_specific)
top2000_go_with_categories |> count(transition, transition_specific)

glimpse(top1000_go_with_categories)
glimpse(top2000_go_with_categories)
```


## Create Excel Workbook

```{r}
#| label: create-excel

# Start timing
tic("Excel creation")

# Create a workbook
wb <- wb_workbook() |>
  wb_set_bookview(window_height = 100000L, window_width = 100000L)

# Add GO results for top 1000 CG sites
suppl_data_order <- 7
top1000_legend <- glue("Data S{suppl_data_order}. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis results for the top 1000 CpG sites. The analysis was performed using the clusterProfiler R package. Only GO terms with adjusted P < 0.05 are shown. The columns represent: 
- transition: dementia transition type
- ID: Gene Ontology term identifier
- Description: Biological process description of the GO term
- GeneRatio: Number of genes from input list in this GO term divided by the number of input genes in the background, that is, with at least one GO biological process annotation
- BgRatio: Number of genes in this GO term in the background divided by total number of background genes
- RichFactor: Fraction of all known genes in this pathway found in the data (calculated as number of genes in pathway divided by number of genes in pathway background)
- FoldEnrichment: How many times more frequent the pathway is in the gene list compared to background
- zScore: Statistical measure of enrichment strength (higher absolute values indicate stronger enrichment)
- pvalue: Raw P value from the Fisher's exact test (lower values indicate stronger statistical significance)
- p.adjust: P value adjusted for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg method (controls false discovery rate)
- qvalue: Another type of adjusted P value (similar to p.adjust but less conservative)
- geneID: List of genes from the input that belong to this GO term (separated by '/')
- Count: Number of genes from the input list in this GO term
- transition_specific: significant in only one group ('Yes' or 'No'); 'Removed' for a parent term whose genes are identical to those of a significant child term, which was not counted (the child is named in duplicate_of)
- duplicate_of: for a removed parent term, the GO identifier of the child term with the same genes
- n_relatives: number of immediate relatives (parent and child terms, all relation types) of a transition-specific term in the GO graph
- n_relatives_same_group: number of these relatives that are significant in the same group
- n_relatives_other_group: number of these relatives that are significant in another group
- n_relatives_significant: number of these relatives that are significant in any group (a relative significant in both the same and another group is counted once)
- specificity_weight: redundancy-aware weight, 1 − n_relatives_significant / n_relatives (1 for a term with no significant immediate relative); the counts of transition-specific terms per group and per functional category are sums of these weights, rounded to whole numbers
- biofunc_category: The biological function category assigned to the GO term (if transition-specific)") |> 
  as.character()

wb <- wb |> 
  add_go_to_excel(
    df = top1000_go_with_categories, 
    sheet_name = "GO_top1000", 
    legend = top1000_legend
  )

# Add GO results for top 2000 CG sites
suppl_data_order <- 8
top2000_legend <- glue("Data S{suppl_data_order}. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis results for the top 2000 CpG sites. The analysis was performed using the clusterProfiler R package. Only GO terms with adjusted P < 0.05 are shown. The columns represent: 
- transition: dementia transition type
- ID: Gene Ontology term identifier
- Description: Biological process description of the GO term
- GeneRatio: Number of genes from input list in this GO term divided by the number of input genes in the background, that is, with at least one GO biological process annotation
- BgRatio: Number of genes in this GO term in the background divided by total number of background genes
- RichFactor: Fraction of all known genes in this pathway found in the data (calculated as number of genes in pathway divided by number of genes in pathway background)
- FoldEnrichment: How many times more frequent the pathway is in the gene list compared to background
- zScore: Statistical measure of enrichment strength (higher absolute values indicate stronger enrichment)
- pvalue: Raw P value from the Fisher's exact test (lower values indicate stronger statistical significance)
- p.adjust: P value adjusted for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg method (controls false discovery rate)
- qvalue: Another type of adjusted P value (similar to p.adjust but less conservative)
- geneID: List of genes from the input that belong to this GO term (separated by '/')
- Count: Number of genes from the input list in this GO term
- transition_specific: significant in only one group ('Yes' or 'No'); 'Removed' for a parent term whose genes are identical to those of a significant child term, which was not counted (the child is named in duplicate_of)
- duplicate_of: for a removed parent term, the GO identifier of the child term with the same genes
- n_relatives: number of immediate relatives (parent and child terms, all relation types) of a transition-specific term in the GO graph
- n_relatives_same_group: number of these relatives that are significant in the same group
- n_relatives_other_group: number of these relatives that are significant in another group
- n_relatives_significant: number of these relatives that are significant in any group (a relative significant in both the same and another group is counted once)
- specificity_weight: redundancy-aware weight, 1 − n_relatives_significant / n_relatives (1 for a term with no significant immediate relative); the counts of transition-specific terms per group and per functional category are sums of these weights, rounded to whole numbers
- biofunc_category: The biological function category assigned to the GO term (if transition-specific)") |> 
  as.character()

wb <- wb |> 
  add_go_to_excel(
    df = top2000_go_with_categories, 
    sheet_name = "GO_top2000", 
    legend = top2000_legend
  )

# Save the workbook
fs::dir_create(here("extended_data/output"))
output_file <- here("extended_data/output/go_enrichment_results.xlsx")
wb |> wb_save(output_file)

# End timing
toc()

cat(glue("Excel file saved to: {output_file}\n"))
```

## Summary

This document has created an Excel workbook with two sheets:
1. GO_top1000 - Gene Ontology enrichment results for the top 1000 CG sites
2. GO_top2000 - Gene Ontology enrichment results for the top 2000 CG sites

Each sheet contains the significant GO terms (adjusted p-value < 0.05) formatted according to the specifications in the `add_go_to_excel` function.
